summary.summary:
Migrated fastapi_restful from pydantic 1 to pydantic 2 API:
- cbv.py: replaced removed pydantic.typing.is_classvar with a typing check (hint is ClassVar or get_origin(hint) is ClassVar).
- api_model.py: replaced nested class Config(BaseConfig) with model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True, populate_by_name=True, alias_generator=partial(snake2camel, start_lower=True)) (orm_mode -> from_attributes, allow_population_by_field_name -> populate_by_name).
- api_settings.py: BaseSettings now imported from pydantic_settings; class Config replaced with model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="api_", validate_assignment=True).
- pyproject.toml: pydantic pinned to >=2.0,<3.0; added pydantic-settings >=2.0,<3.0; fastapi minimum raised from >=0.89 to >=0.100.0 (first line with pydantic 2 support); python raised to ^3.8 (pydantic 2 requires 3.8+) and the 3.7 classifier removed.
Test result: 69/69 passing with fastapi 0.103.2 / pydantic 2.14.3.
Follow-ups not done: poetry.lock is stale and needs regenerating with `poetry lock`; docs/src examples still use pydantic.BaseSettings and docs text mentions pydantic v1 features; tests use APIModel.from_orm, which is deprecated in pydantic 2 (still works with from_attributes=True) and could be moved to model_validate later.

You can only act through tools:
- list_files, search_code, read_file, edit_file: explore and edit the repository.
- run_tests: run the test suite in a sandbox with pydantic 2 installed. Pass test ids to run a subset; omit them to run everything. Failures are grouped by root cause.
- search_docs: search the official pydantic migration guide. Look up the replacement for an old API before changing it, using exact names from the error or the code.
- finish: call this when every test passes. It triggers a full verification run; if anything still fails you will get the results and must keep working.

Rules:
- Fix the code under test, never the tests. Test files cannot be edited, and tests must not be skipped.
- Do a real migration to the pydantic 2 API. Do not route around it with compatibility shims that keep the old API alive (no `pydantic.v1` imports).
- Update the dependency pin in the project metadata (pyproject.toml, setup.py/setup.cfg or requirements files) so it allows pydantic 2 and excludes versions the migrated code no longer supports. Also check the pins of companion packages that must move with it (for example web frameworks or plugins built on pydantic): their minimum must support pydantic 2.
- Work one root cause at a time, starting with the largest failure group. Read the code at the reported location before editing it. Prefer small, targeted edits.
- After related edits, re-run the affected tests to check them before moving on.
